title: Examining user behavior with machine learning for effective mobile peer-to-peer payment adoption
authors: Antonio, B.O.; Juan, L.R.; Ana, I.D.; Francisco, L.C.
tldr: Machine learning classifiers combined with Boruta feature selection predict mobile P2P payment adoption, identifying perceived usefulness, subjective norms, trust, and enjoyment as the strongest predictors among Spanish Bizum users.
problem_and_motivation: Understanding the drivers and barriers of mobile peer-to-peer payment adoption remains critical for financial institutions, yet traditional parametric methods may fail to capture nonlinear relationships among behavioral variables. Existing research lacks comparative evidence on whether nonparametric machine learning approaches outperform classical techniques for classifying mobile P2P payment users. Feature selection as preprocessing for high-dimensional adoption data has not been systematically evaluated in this domain.
approach: Surveyed 701 Spanish smartphone users about Bizum mobile P2P payment adoption, yielding a dataset with 42 behavioral and demographic predictor variables.
Applied Boruta and Gini index feature selection procedures to reduce dimensionality from 42 to 8 variables while preserving classification signal.
Compared parametric methods (LDA, QDA, logistic regression) against nonparametric ML algorithms (RF, MLP, SVM, CART, bagging, boosting variants).
Evaluated all models using multiple metrics: sensitivity, specificity, G-mean, AUC, discriminant power, balanced accuracy, Youden's index, and a composite Global Performance Index.
Used tenfold cross-validation throughout for hyperparameter tuning and error estimation across all algorithms.
findings: num: Binomial boosting achieved the best GPI score of 0.6859, followed by MLP4 (0.6613) and L2 boosting (0.6609).
num: Feature selection reduced variables from 42 to 8 (19.04% of original features), consistently improving performance across all methods.
num: MLP1 and MLP2 achieved the highest AUC values, followed closely by SVM and L2 boosting.
Nonparametric ML techniques generally outperform classical LDA and logistic regression for classifying mobile P2P payment users.
Perceived usefulness (PU) variables are the strongest predictors of mobile P2P payment adoption, followed by subjective norms, trust, and enjoyment.
CART and CTBag (bagged trees) obtained the worst performance in terms of GPI, highlighting limitations of single-tree approaches.
Boruta and Gini index procedures show strong agreement in the top-ranked variables, confirming robustness of the feature selection.
Maximum VIF value of 6.548 (PU2) confirms absence of multicollinearity problems among selected variables.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper contributes to the financial technology and machine learning literature by demonstrating that nonparametric ML methods outperform traditional parametric approaches for predicting consumer adoption of mobile P2P payments. It provides a rigorous comparative evaluation of 16 classification algorithms, introducing a composite Global Performance Index that synthesizes multiple performance metrics. The study identifies perceived usefulness, subjective norms, perceived trust, and perceived enjoyment as the four strongest behavioral predictors of mobile P2P payment adoption, ordered by classification importance. The paper also demonstrates that Boruta-based feature selection reduces dimensionality from 42 to 8 variables while improving model performance across all algorithms, establishing a practical preprocessing pipeline for high-dimensional financial behavioral data.
directly_justifies: Nonparametric ML techniques consistently outperform classical LDA and logistic regression for classifying mobile P2P payment users.
Feature selection via Boruta and Gini index reduces variables from 42 to 8 while improving prediction across all methods.
Binomial boosting achieves the highest Global Performance Index score of 0.6859 among all tested classifiers.
Perceived usefulness is the strongest predictor, followed by subjective norms, trust, and enjoyment of using mobile P2P payments.
Boruta and Gini index procedures show strong agreement in top variable rankings, confirming robustness of the dual feature selection approach.
limits: Study is limited to the Spanish population and Bizum platform, restricting cross-cultural generalizability.
Uses nonprobability snowball sampling, which may introduce selection bias and limit external validity.
Dataset lacks information on users' technology training, educational background, and risk aversion as moderating variables.
No analysis of how transaction size or risk aversion influences adoption of mobile P2P payments.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned for relevance. Domain 4 (Landscape) was flagged as medium relevance because the paper provides an extensive review of existing mobile payment systems and prior adoption research. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was flagged as high relevance for both behavioral profile analysis (5.A) and classification approaches (5.C), as the paper's core contribution is identifying and classifying behavioral attributes that predict payment adoption. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as high relevance (6.A) because the paper applies multiple ML algorithms to predict user adoption. Domain 10 (Data Privacy/Security) was assigned medium relevance to 10.B (User Trust) because perceived trust is a significant adoption predictor, though the paper does not address privacy architecture or consent. Domain 12 (Evaluation Frameworks) was flagged as medium for 12.A and high for 12.B due to the comprehensive algorithmic comparison methodology. Borderline cases considered and rejected include 2.C (User-Declared Financial Preferences), as the survey measures attitudes rather than declared allocation preferences; 9.B (Mobile UX Design), as the paper discusses payment system features but not mobile UX design principles; and 11.A (Engagement Dynamics), as user intention is measured but not ongoing engagement behavior. Domains 1 (Filipino demographics), 3 (Expense Categorization), 7 (Budgeting), 8 (Anomaly Detection), 13 (Savings/Debt), and 14 (Synthetic Data/Deployment) were considered and rejected as outside the paper's scope.

limitations: Study confined to Spanish population and Bizum platform, limiting cross-cultural generalizability.
Nonprobability snowball sampling may introduce selection bias.
Dataset lacks moderating variables such as technology training, education level, and risk aversion. [unacknowledged]
No analysis of transaction size or its interaction with risk aversion in adoption decisions.
ML implementation involves subjective choices among manifold options, potential data bias and drift, and black-box interpretability challenges.
